runs.name: FUJIFILM Holdings Corporation
runs.box: TOO HARD (NATURE) AT Q2; integrity facts recorded, not judged
runs.entry: Price **¥3,402** (TSE 4901, labelled by the analyst the close of 2026-10-13 JST; the dispatcher notes the run was written about 10:30 JST that day, so the quote is intraday, not a close; prior close ¥3,427 on 2026-10-09, Tokyo shut 2026-10-12) and ADR **$10.77** (OTC 2026-10-12), aggregator, flagged; **1 ADS = 1/2 share** on the depositaries' F-6 POS filings (Deutsche Bank 0001104659-24-040381, Citibank 0001193805-24-000467, both unsponsored), checked from the two quotes at ¥158.44. Shares **1,195,607,779** (issued 1,234,150,284 less treasury 38,542,505 at 2026-06-30, Q1 FY2026 release of 2026-08-06; the April 2026 buyback of 9,726,900 shares cancelled 2026-06-30) = cap **¥4,067.5bn** ($25.7bn); sovereign **4.14%** (JGB 30Y, Ministry of Finance, 2026-10-08). Not an SEC registrant (EDGAR CIK 1537075 holds only tender-offer and ownership filings as a bidder): `tools/run.py` and `cover_shares.py` returned nothing; every figure by hand from the company's US GAAP results releases filed with the TSE (years ended March 2016 to March 2026, Q1 FY2026) and Integrated Reports 2025 and 2021; operating cash ¥428,162m (FY2024) cross-checked in three documents. The annual securities report (yuho) was not read. Lines of evidence derived by the analyst from the company's own reports, as the overnight brief directs. **Q1 IN, narrowly**, on the deciding part: Imaging at 31% of five-year segment operating income (¥511bn of FY2021-25; Healthcare 27%, Electronics 22%, Business Innovation 20%). **Q2 TOO HARD (NATURE)**: Imaging's margin 5.5% to 14.6% over FY2014-20 with revenue down 26% in two years, 25.5% in FY2025, operating income ¥56bn (FY2017) to ¥15.6bn (FY2020) to ¥160bn (FY2025); a change for the better that section C credits only after a full cycle, untested by a fall in volume, part of it possibly the yen (¥106 to ¥151); re-look at the first fiscal year in which Imaging revenue, or instax or camera units, fall. Q3 to Q12 not reached. After the stop, recorded not weighed: the Fuji Xerox New Zealand and Australia accounting corrections (FY2010 to Q3 FY2016, Independent Investigation Committee) and a further ¥10.1bn correction in FY2017; Healthcare a ¥12.7bn loss in the June 2026 quarter on Bio CDMO fixed costs; free cash after all capital spending negative four years running (¥-121, -41, -118, -170bn FY2022-25); construction in progress ¥980bn; ROIC 5.5%; the 2026-08-06 notice of an assessment of a partial spin-off of Business Innovation; the April 2026 buyback at an average ¥3,084. COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE: owner cash, five-year average FY2021-25, ¥-60bn after all capital spending, ¥204bn maintenance case, ¥172bn default central after acquisitions; value range **¥2,657 to ¥2,826 a share ($8.38 to $8.92 per ADS)** against ¥3,402 (the growth case below the no-growth case, spending above depreciation averaging ¥264bn a year); no case earns the floor (no-growth cash 3.55% of an enterprise value of ¥4,847bn); fair price beneath the stop **¥372 all-equity ($1.17 per ADS)**, ¥984 equity-only ($3.11); organic pair beside ¥3,515 and ¥4,269 (fair ¥1,073 and ¥540); literal window all spending ¥-1,820; not armed (box not OUT at Q7). Balance sheets: cash ¥876bn (2017) to ¥151bn, debt ¥366bn to ¥976bn, net debt about ¥780bn; net plant quadrupled in five years; goodwill ¥997bn; ¥0.7tn of equity is currency translation; inventories up 72% against revenue up 36%. Competitors: the company's reports name none; the analyst chose Canon (20-F, the only usable SEC filer; camera unit margin 1.1% in 2020, 15.8% in 2022; no 20-F after 2022); Sony (cameras not reported separately), Kodak (not read), Polaroid, Nikon and OM Digital (not SEC filers) flagged. Contamination declared by the analyst: a `ls` of `Test Runs/` filtered on 'fuji' printed the file names of the 2026-07-15 FUJIY and FJTSY runs (a breach of the blind rule's 'do not list', declared and left unticked in the self-audit; neither opened), the session's NPNYY commit subjects and a memory index line; none used. Commits 0721e8ce, 8afe52e5, 6ff0f9f3, 88ddf46d. Citations: the analyst's check no E-ids, 36 distinct ids, 11 fragments matched; the dispatcher's adjacency script 37 ids resolved, 10 adjacent fragments, 0 slips. Position note filled at the fold. check_framework PASS. **For the operator:** the analyst's gaps: (1) Q2 section B's 'largest part decides' made Imaging decide at 31%, though it was the smallest segment every year through FY2020 and most of the capital sits in Bio CDMO; the framework is silent where the largest part is a minority and only recently the largest; (2) Q1's earning-power test and Q2 section C overlap for a change for the better, so the same facts could close at Q1 TOO HARD (NATURE), the box the same, the door not fixed; (3) section C's re-look assumes a volume series the company does not publish; (4) Q7 (e) does not say whether growth spending stops when growth stops, which here inverts the range; (5) the serial-acquirer test is undefined when owner cash before purchases is negative.
runs.narr: Q2 TOO HARD (NATURE): a four-segment group whose largest part by five-year profit is Imaging at 31% (instax and cameras), its margin 25.5% in FY2025 against 5.5% to 14.6% over FY2014-20; a change for the better not yet tested by a fall in volume, part of it possibly the yen; re-look at the first year Imaging revenue or units fall. Q1 passed narrowly. COMPUTATION beneath the stop: range ¥2,657 to ¥2,826 at the 4.14% JGB against ¥3,402, no case earns the floor, fair ¥372 all-equity (¥984 equity-only), not armed. After the stop: the Fuji Xerox accounting corrections of 2017-18; free cash negative four years on the Bio CDMO build-out, ¥980bn under construction, net debt about ¥780bn; a partial spin-off of Business Innovation under assessment.
